Reads access_token and expiry_date only; never refresh_token, never writes the file, contains no Google token endpoint, grant type or refresh token. An access token past its expiry_date is an AuthFailure raised before any request. No currentTier means refused: the feeder never calls onboardUser.

Title: Gemini token keeper
Detail: Runs gemini --acp and sends initialize then authenticate{oauth-personal} and nothing else, so the CLI's own refreshAuth renews the token with no model call (gemini -p /stats is rejected: headless mode sends the text to the model). Refuses before starting when settings.auth.selectedType is not oauth-personal (authenticate would clear the cached credentials) or when no cached credential exists (it would begin an interactive login). Prints one status line and nothing the CLI said. 4-minute timer, because google-auth-library renews only inside its 5-minute eager window (interval plus AccuracySec plus RandomizedDelaySec must stay under it); 60 s self-bound, 90 s unit bound, no stacking. NOT PROVEN against a live CLI.

Title: Codex error message surfaced and redacted
Detail: The failure text is 'codex: JSON-RPC error <code>: <message and data>' with Bearer values, JWTs, vendor key prefixes and 24+ character opaque runs replaced by [redacted] BEFORE truncation to 200 characters, and control characters flattened. token_expired (or '401 Unauthorized' / status 401) yields an AuthFailure; anything else a SourceFailure; a non-object error still fails closed.

Title: Typed authentication failure and its classification
Detail: AuthFailure(SourceFailure) carries status and code. An HTTP 401 is one; 403/404/429/5xx are not. 'carries no usable key' is raised as NoUsableKey (plain everywhere) and promoted to AuthFailure only inside the Claude readers. run_cycle catches AuthFailure before SourceFailure; no reader catches a SourceFailure and re-raises a plain one.

Title: Consecutive-failure count in the state file
Detail: One reserved key (__auth_failures__) maps source to a small integer, capped at AUTH_CONFIRM_CYCLES; load_state validates it with its own validator (known sources, ints 1..100) and run_cycle writes it back through save_state. A success, a non-auth failure or a disabled source has no entry, which is the reset. Counts and timestamps only.

Title: Auth marker: grey and sticky with the optional gauge intact
Detail: On the confirming cycle each stored reading (or corrupt entry) of the source is replaced by {auth_failed: true, at} under the SAME key, which load_state validates separately; build_post treats a marker as no usable reading and takes an auth_confirmed flag that skips the stored reading regardless. A gauge never posted is not marked. A real reading overwrites the marker. The key is kept so state_keys still reports an optional gauge as seen.

Title: Sign-in guidance printed by setup
Detail: Prints claude auth login --claudeai (never claude setup-token, whose token lacks user:profile), the account 2 command with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and the Gemini command with NO_BROWSER=true, for the sources named in AI_USAGE_SOURCES.

Title: Knobs documented
Detail: Every AI_USAGE_* knob in .env.example except the feeder's plumbing appears in docs/config-reference.md with its default and meaning; the example AI_USAGE_SOURCES line is claude,claude2,codex,gemini,opencode while the absent-knob default stays codex,claude,opencode; the reload steps are recorded.

Title: Weight feeder: typed AuthFailure from the Google token refresh
Detail: The token refresh (and only the refresh) raises AuthFailure, a SourceFailure subclass carrying the status or the allow-listed OAuth word, for HTTP 401 and for HTTP 400 whose OAuth error is invalid_grant. Every other status, every other 400, a 403, a 5xx, a transport error and a 401 from the list call stay plain SourceFailure, so a wrong OAuth client or a missing scope never greys the gauge. run_cycle catches AuthFailure before SourceFailure and keeps the class.

Title: Weight feeder: logging invariant amended narrowly for the OAuth error word
Detail: Nothing the remote wrote reaches a message except one matched constant: for the token refresh only, the top-level error member of the JSON body is compared by equality against AUTH_ERROR_ALLOWLIST (invalid_grant) and the allow-list entry itself is returned. error_description, quoted headers, non-string or differently shaped error members, near-misses by case or whitespace and oversized bodies are never read into a message. The body read is bounded.

Title: Weight feeder: two consecutive sign-in failures confirm a dead login
CodeSymbol: weight_feeder.AUTH_STATE_KEY; weight_feeder.AUTH_CONFIRM_CYCLES; weight_feeder.validate_auth_counts; weight_feeder.load_state; weight_feeder.save_state; weight_feeder.run_cycle
Detail: A per-source count of consecutive sign-in-failed cycles lives in the state file under the reserved key auth-failed-cycles, because the service is a one-shot timer. load_state gives it a dedicated validator (known source name, real integer, at least 1, clamped to 2; any other member dropped alone) as it does for the checked and inches keys, and save_state carries it. Any cycle that is not a sign-in failure removes the count. The count holds integers only, never a credential or a response body. The gauge greys on the second consecutive failed cycle, up to about 30 minutes after the login dies.

Title: Weight feeder: a confirmed dead login posts the never-measured body and the grey sticks
Detail: build_post takes an auth_failed flag that skips the stored-reading branch and returns gauge_body(0.0, goal, None): value 0, no observed_at, stale on arrival. On the confirming cycle run_cycle passes the flag and clears the stored weight reading from the state file (the weight gauge is not optional, so clearing is correct), so any later failure of any kind finds nothing to re-post and stays stale on arrival. The first failed cycle behaves as before. A network failure with no sign-in failure still re-posts the last reading at its original stamp. A real reading after the login is renewed rewrites the entry and posts live.

Title: Weight feeder: operator hint names 400 invalid_grant and the 7-day Testing cliff
Detail: The hint on a dead refresh token says it is no longer valid, to run weight_oauth.py mint --force, and that an OAuth app left in Testing expires the token every 7 days (fix: publish to In production). The incorrect claim that a 401 is what signals this is removed; the 403 scope hint is kept. The README troubleshooting tables and the mint section state the 400 invalid_grant meaning and the 7-day cliff.

Title: Weight feeder: waist-to-height sister gauge not greyed is a documented known limit
Detail: The weight-waist gauge has no unavailable body, so a confirmed dead weight login does not grey it; it keeps its cached halves at their original stamps until the NagLight static 7-day horizon. This is stated in the README rather than worked around.

Title: Wall capability contract is a floor over the panel's own capabilities.json
Detail: The release gate used to pin the whole capability manifest exactly, so every panel change had to be mirrored by hand and the pin drifted: by 2026-10-11 OfficeWallNaglight CameraOpt declared seven capabilities and four expanded file lists the pin had never heard of, and the image path that calls it would have refused any current artifact. REQUIRED is now a FLOOR. The manifest must be schema 2, must still declare every floor capability, and each floor capability must still declare every floor file in every payload; anything the manifest declares beyond the floor is accepted. Removing or shrinking a floor capability still fails. The floor is the CameraOpt de85047 manifest (22 capabilities).

Title: Every file the manifest declares must be in the archive and well formed
Detail: A declaration alone cannot satisfy a capability, and that now holds for capabilities beyond the floor too: every file the payload's own manifest declares for that payload is required to be a non-empty regular member, each capability must carry exactly the app/gateway/site keys as duplicate-free lists of safe relative paths (no absolute, backslash or dot-dot), and build-info.json must list exactly the manifest's capability names.

Title: The public site inventory stays exact and names every offender
Detail: The hub extracts the site archive into a public document root, so an extra file is an extra HTTP response surface and the inventory is NOT derived from the manifest. It stays an exact allow-list in both directions (an unlisted file and a listed-but-absent file are both refused), now includes the 27 files the panel had added since it was last updated (CameraOpt de85047, 74 files), and a refusal names every offending file (first twelve, then a count) so one run shows the whole job.

Title: A panel change costs the gate one inventory line at most, and growth is visible
Detail: Adding a capability, or a file to a capability, needs no edit to the gate; adding a file to the public site payload needs one line in ALLOWED_SITE_FILES. When the manifest has grown past the floor the CLI prints a NOTE per addition and still passes, so drift is reported without blocking a release. The gate is exercised against a read-only copy of the panel's own manifest and site file list (tests/fixtures/wall-camera-opt, taken from CameraOpt de85047) and against mutations of it. NOT exercised here: the vmtest image path that calls the script (needs the lab).

Title: Sleep feeder: own account, private state directory, one writable file
Detail: A oneshot unit on a 30-minute timer, User=homehub-sleep with no home (useradd --no-create-home, written into a drop-in from SLEEP_USER_ACCOUNT, hub and root refused), StateDirectory=homehub-sleep mode 0700, ReadWritePaths of that directory only, ProtectHome=yes, and the same hardening directives as the weight unit (compared directive by directive by test). The only file ever opened for writing is the state file or its .tmp sibling: the resolved path must sit inside the service's own state directory AND equal one of those two paths, it is created O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW at mode 0600 after unlinking any planted link, and a path outside either is a PermissionError. The unit is ordered After= and Wants= time-sync.target, because night keys, the noon stamp and the 14:00 rule are local dates read off the host clock.

Title: Sleep feeder: identity, loopback destination, no redirect, no proxy
Detail: SLEEP_USER blank is a refusal. SLEEP_FEED_URL must be http/https with an IP-literal host that is loopback or inside a network a docker0/br-* bridge carries; a hostname is refused unresolved. The POST opener installs no proxy, raises on every 3xx without re-sending, and asks the connected socket for its peer address before a byte of the request is written. X-Forwarded-User carries the identity; Authorization is sent only when SLEEP_FEED_TOKEN is set; the remote's response body is never put in the returned detail.

Title: Sleep feeder: off by default, publish by default, 0 is an off switch
Detail: Only a literal SLEEP_ENABLED=true runs the feeder. SLEEP_PUBLISH defaults to 1; 0, false, no and off (any case) make main return 0 after --check has validated the configuration, with nothing read, nothing posted and no state file written. Blank, 1 and any other value publish.

Title: Sleep feeder: the journal carries status only
Detail: Every journal line is the feeder's own text: which source answered, the night key, 'published night <key>', and failure lines with at most an allow-listed status word. No score, sub-score, usage figure, credential, email, token or response body is ever formatted into a message, an exception or the state file's non-night keys. Tested by running distinctive scores and a password sentinel through the real cycle and the real reader and scanning stdout, stderr and the state file.

Title: Sleep feeder: the gauge on the wire
Detail: {kind gauge, id sleep, label Sleep, icon sleep, unit pts, value, min 0, max 100, target 80, favourable high, window {kind daily}, observed_at} and nothing else: no start, end, direction, previous_value or previous_observed_at. observed_at is RFC3339 with the zone's offset for that instant. The unavailable body is the same with value 0 and no observed_at. The key set is checked against the JSON tags of NagLight's gauge struct when a sibling checkout exists.

Title: Sleep feeder: night key is startDate plus one calendar day
Detail: startDate must be a strict bare YYYY-MM-DD (anything else is unreadable and skipped, and counted in the journal); the night key is that date plus one calendar day by date arithmetic, so a month, year, leap day or DST change cannot move it. A record whose night key is in the future neither publishes nor blocks today's night.

Title: Sleep feeder: only a finite score within 0..100 is a score; never a manufactured zero
Detail: A finite int or float in 0..100 inclusive is a score, whole floats become ints, and myAir's own 0 is published as 0. None, a missing key, a string, a bool, NaN, an infinity and an out-of-range number are no data: no entry is created, none is erased, and the gauge falls to the unavailable rules. Two records for one night with different valid scores are skipped for that cycle.

Title: Sleep feeder: one entry per night, upserted; a correction never moves observed_at
Detail: A night first seen is stored with its score and stamp; a later fetch with a different valid score replaces the score and leaves the stamp; a later null, missing, invalid or absent score NEVER ERASES a published night - it creates no entry, deletes none and changes no value. Only the expected night and the previous night are ever stored and the state is pruned to three days back.

Title: Sleep feeder: observed_at is the earlier of noon local and first publication, frozen
Detail: A new night is stamped min(12:00 local on the night-key date, now). A record arriving at 07:00 is stamped 07:00; one arriving after noon is stamped noon and never the fetch time. The expected night is never first published before 06:00 local: a record found earlier is staged with its stamp floored at 06:00 on its own date, so the stamp lands in the right NagLight tracking day (02:00 boundary). The stamp is set once, survives restarts, and the loader drops any stored stamp later than noon on its night-key date, in the future, or before the block existed.

Title: Sleep feeder: the expected night and the 14:00 local rule
Detail: The expected night is today's local date. With the expected night stored it is shown. Without it, before 14:00 local the previous night's stored score is shown at its own frozen stamp; from 14:00 local, or with nothing PUBLISHED for the previous night, the unavailable body is posted. 13:59:59 is before the boundary and 14:00:00 is after it, on ordinary days and on the 23- and 25-hour days.

Title: Sleep feeder: an old night is never shown as last night
Detail: Only the exact expected night key, or before the grace hour the exact previous night key AND ONLY IF THE FEEDER PUBLISHED IT (a separate published set in the state file, recorded when the tracker accepted a body carrying that night's score; a night merely fetched or staged after an outage or a confirmed dead-login period is not one), can be shown. After an outage from 10-10 to 10-13 a recovery at 09:00 returning only night key 10-12 posts unavailable, not 10-12. A published key later than today + 1 day is dropped on load with a status line; --retry-now also clears keys later than today. Once today's night has been published, no earlier night is selected for display that day: if today's record is unavailable (for example quarantined after a same-day backwards clock step) the unavailable body is posted, not yesterday's score. An observation stamped in the future is quarantined - kept, not displayed, reconsidered when the clock passes it. A newest record two or more nights old posts the unavailable body at every hour of the day, and stored nights older than the previous one are never selected.

Title: Sleep feeder: the TIMEZONE knob and DST-safe arithmetic
Detail: TIMEZONE blank or unknown is a refusal naming the knob. Etc/UTC and UTC need no tz database; other names need zoneinfo. Local dates and hours are read off the zone's own offset for the instant (fromtimestamp), and noon is built from the date and the zone. The clock is read AGAIN after the fetch, before selecting and posting (a cycle that starts at 13:59 and ends at 14:01 applies the 14:00 rule), and a local date earlier than the newest published night means the clock went backwards: nothing is fetched, selected or posted and the journal says so, status only. Before anything is fetched or posted the host clock must be shown synchronised: systemd-timesyncd's flag file /run/systemd/timesync/synchronized (the hub's method), else timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized --value with a 5 s timeout; if neither is available or the clock is not synchronised the cycle fetches nothing and publishes no timestamped score but still POSTS THE UNAVAILABLE BODY (no observed_at) on every such tick, reads and writes no state, and logs a status line naming systemd-timesyncd and timedatectl; setup-sleep.sh prints one install-time line saying which signal exists. Night keys dated later than tomorrow are pruned from the nights as from the published set. So noon on a spring-forward day is 17:00Z and on a fall-back day 18:00Z in US Central; no calculation adds 24 hours.

Title: Sleep feeder: the state file is validated, private and survives a restart
Detail: The state file holds {nights, published, schedule, __auth_failures__, __auth_failed__}: night keys with a score and a frozen stamp, the published night keys, the last-asked memory of the fetch windows, a failure count and a sticky marker (with an optional allow-listed status code), each parsed by its own validator and dropped when not credible (the next save would erase it), except that a night stamped in the future is kept and quarantined rather than dropped. It is written atomically through the write guard at mode 0600, never holds a credential, token, header or body, and after a restart the same stamps are republished and nothing is posted as fresher than it was.

Title: Sleep feeder: the sign-in is the observed flow on the standard library
Detail: GET authorize (a 400 that hands out the device cookie), POST authn with the email and password as JSON, GET authorize with the session token and an S256 challenge (a 302 whose Location fragment carries the code, never followed), POST token as a form with the verifier, then one POST to the GraphQL endpoint with x-api-key, the bearer token and the country claim of the id token. Production URLs must be https and a vendor 3xx is never followed. The query asks for the last 30 days and only startDate and sleepScore. An absent items list is a failure; an empty one is none. myAir is asked only when fetch_due says so: while the expected night is not stored, between 06:00 and 16:00 local and at most once per two hours; once stored, one correction re-fetch from 14:30 and one from 20:00 local (each at most once per local day); on the next tick after a first refusal; at 20:00 local even if the night is still missing (one late-upload catch-up a day, so a 16:00-20:00 upload is published that evening; a later upload is staged next morning but, never published, shows unavailable until the new night arrives), and after a confirmed dead login only when the back-off has elapsed and only between 06:00 and 22:00 local. A slot is marked done only after a read that did not fail; a failed non-authentication read is retried at most twice more, 30 minutes apart, none from 22:00, and attempt_at is recorded regardless. Every tick still posts from stored state. A normal day is about five sign-ins.

Title: Sleep feeder: the sign-in values are held for one cycle and never shown
Detail: MYAIR_EMAIL and MYAIR_PASSWORD blank is a refusal that names the knob and echoes neither. The materialiser's doubled dollar is collapsed in the password (a single dollar is left alone). The password appears in exactly one request body, in no header, URL, exception, journal line or state file; transport failures name the exception type only.

Title: Sleep feeder: authentication failures are typed and nothing else is
Detail: An Okta 401 at authn or token, an authn status other than SUCCESS (reported only as an allow-listed word, else UNRECOGNISED), a GraphQL 401 and a GraphQL unauthorized error are AuthFailure; MFA_REQUIRED is the subtype MfaRequired. A 5xx, 403, 429, 400, a timeout, a refused connection, a missing field and a malformed body are plain SourceFailure. No code catches an AuthFailure and re-raises it as a plain one, and the per-source handler catches AuthFailure first.

Title: Sleep feeder: two consecutive authentication failures, counted in the state file
Detail: The first authentication failure behaves as today: the last stored score is re-posted at its original stamp. The second consecutive one posts the unavailable body. The count lives under the reserved key __auth_failures__ with its own validator (int 1..100, one source), is capped at the threshold, survives a restart, and is reset by any non-authentication outcome of an ATTEMPT, success or failure; a tick on which myAir was not asked is not an outcome and resets nothing.

Title: Sleep feeder: a confirmed dead login is sticky; MFA is a message, never a mailbox
Detail: On confirmation a marker {auth_failed, at} is stored under __auth_failed__ with its own validator. While it is present every cycle posts the unavailable body, including after a network failure, until a read succeeds, which clears it and the count. While it is set myAir is NOT ASKED AT ALL (zero Okta calls, the wall stays grey from stored state) for 6 h after the last refusal, or 24 h when the failing authn status was LOCKED_OUT; one attempt then follows, and a refusal restarts the back-off from itself. --retry-now clears the marker and the count and asks at once, outside the windows and the back-off; the operator runs it under the unit's account with systemd-run. It refuses (one-line reason, exit 2) when the effective uid is 0 or the state file is owned by another user, and it also clears published keys dated later than today. MFA_REQUIRED logs 'myAir now asks for an emailed code - a person must sign in (see refresh-gauge-logins)', makes no factor call, and goes through the same confirmation; the module imports no mail library and uses no mail class.

Title: Heart gauge: opt-in, validated knobs, and the exact wire body
Detail: HEART_ENABLED is on only for a literal 1 or true and defaults to 0; off means run_heart_cycle returns at once with no read, no post and no state write. HEART_MIN_BPM, HEART_MAX_BPM and HEART_TARGET_BPM (40, 100, 60) are whole numbers inside 1..300 with MIN < MAX and MIN <= TARGET <= MAX, and a bad one is refused naming the knob, never defaulted past. The body is {kind,id=heart,label=Heart,icon=heart,unit=bpm,value,min,max,target,favourable=low,window={kind:daily}[,observed_at]} with no start, end, direction, colour or previous_value; a body carrying observed_at must carry a plausible whole-number rate, so the sentinel 0 only ever travels without a stamp.

Title: Heart gauge: the daily resting heart rate parser, written from the discovery document
Detail: Route /v4/users/me/dataTypes/daily-resting-heart-rate/dataPoints under the existing scope, own token refresh, no filter and no pageSize. A point is read from the dailyRestingHeartRate member: beatsPerMinute must be the plain decimal string (no number, float, sign, padding or non-ASCII digit; matched with fullmatch) inside 25..200, otherwise the point is refused and the message names the field and type and never the value; the latest day wins by date, not position; one bad point costs itself; two disagreeing points for the newest day are refused; name and dataSource are never read. NOT observed against a real body.

Title: Heart gauge: observed_at is the date's own stamp; the stored reading is validated input
Detail: A daily point carries a civil date and no instant, so observed_at is that date at 12:00 LOCAL in the hub's zone (resolve_heart_zone from the TIMEZONE knob; datetime(y, m, d, 12, tzinfo=zone)) so it lands in NagLight's 02:00-local tracking day in CDT, CST and on both DST-change dates; an unset or unknown TIMEZONE is refused with a status line, nothing posted and weight untouched, never guessed as UTC; the stamp is a pure function of the date, unmoved by a later correction and never the clock. A date ahead of the clock by more than the skew but within 48 h is held back (an older day carries the gauge), a date further ahead or before the feeder existed or not a real calendar date is refused. The stored reading lives under the state key heart with its own validator in load_state (resting-rate band, check_observed_at), because the generic validator would accept a heart rate as a body weight; a failed read re-posts it at its ORIGINAL stamp and never marks it fresh.

Title: Heart gauge: no data is unavailable and silent; the sign-in rules are weight's, counted separately
Detail: An account with no resting heart rate (NoWeightYet) posts the stored reading at its original stamp or, with none, value 0 with no observed_at, adds no failure line and writes no state. A sign-in failure is counted under auth-failed-cycles as google-health:heart, separately from weight's google-health; two consecutive confirm, any other outcome (including no data) resets, the confirming cycle clears the stored heart reading so the grey sticks, and the same dead token therefore greys both gauges on the same second cycle without either count being bumped by the other. validate_auth_counts accepts the heart member and drops unknown sources.

Title: Heart gauge: a separate cycle that cannot change weight, and cannot be stopped by it
Detail: run_cycle is unchanged and never calls the heart reader. main runs the heart half after the weight half on every path including a refused one (a missing weight goal does not stop it); a bad heart knob is contained in report_heart, prints a heart: REFUSED line naming the knob and does not alter the weight half. The heart cycle touches only the heart reading and its own count in the state file. Whatever the heart reader does, the weight body and the weight-owned state keys are identical to a run without it, and the reverse.

Title: Heart gauge: the evidence, the operator path and what is not proven are written down
Detail: README section 'Heart (resting heart rate)' states what lights it up, the knobs, that no new consent is needed and how that was checked (the public data-types table lists daily-resting-heart-rate under health_metrics_and_measurements.readonly; discovery revision 20261007 maps no data type to a scope), the stamp rule, the dual-source and unfiltered-call limits, the operator path, and that the parser has not been observed against a real body. weight_oauth.py capture accepts --data-type heart so the first real body can be captured; stack/.env.example documents the four knobs at their defaults.

Title: Sleep feeder first-boot hook: literal-true gate, refusal is a warning
Detail: Step 6f-2 reads SLEEP_ENABLED through _env_val, strips quotes, and tests it against the literal true. It runs `bash $STACK_DIR/sleep/setup-sleep.sh` through the same `| sed` indentation pipe as step 6f; under set -euo pipefail a non-zero exit takes the WARNING branch (which names the reason, already printed above it, and the sudo re-run command) and the script continues to step 6g. A missing script logs that carriage is missing for an activated feature. Nothing is installed or logged when the gate is anything but true.

Title: Sleep feeder payload carriage: tracked files, whole-repo archive, whole-tree copy
CodeSymbol: payload staging (git archive --format=tar HEAD); user-data late-command cp -a
Detail: The six files under stack/sleep/ (README.md, apply-env-lines.py, homehub-sleep.service, homehub-sleep.timer, setup-sleep.sh, sleep_feeder.py) are tracked by git, the payload stager archives HEAD into deploy-payload/, and the installer's late-command copies deploy-payload/. into /opt/homehub/ whole. There is no per-directory list to add stack/sleep/ to, so the test asserts both halves of that statement rather than a list entry.

Title: Sleep and heart knobs: declared names, one template line each, safe defaults
Detail: Every name read through env.get in sleep_feeder.py (SLEEP_*, MYAIR_*) and weight_feeder.py (HEART_*) appears once in stack/.env.example at its documented default. The HomeHub field schema declares them: T0 for the plain knobs, T1 Optional for SLEEP_USER (an identity, tokenised in the hub configuration as the same value as NAGLIGHT_USER), the existing T1 MYAIR_EMAIL and T3 MYAIR_PASSWORD unchanged. The names do not collide with the panel display-sleep knobs SLEEP_MODE, SLEEP_START and SLEEP_END. The hub configuration sets SLEEP_ENABLED=true and SLEEP_USER and does not set HEART_ENABLED. The cross-repo half is asserted by HomeHub's scripts/lab/tests/Deploy.Contracts.Tests.ps1 and is not run by this repository's pytest.

Title: Heart needs no hook; the running-hub procedure is written down
Detail: The weight unit reads /opt/homehub/stack/.env whole and setup-weight.sh neither filters the environment nor mentions HEART_*, so HEART_ENABLED and the three bounds reach the heart reader with no new first-boot code. The sleep README section 'Installing on the RUNNING hub' states that /opt/homehub is not a git checkout, orders the steps (config, .env backup, diff then copy of stack/sleep only, key replacement by apply-env-lines.py that writes atomically (same-directory temp file with the original's mode and owner, fsync, os.replace, directory fsync whose failure after the replace is a warning, flock with an inode re-check, temp removed on failure, stale temps swept under the lock), writes flag keys unquoted so the setup script and first boot (which both strip single and double quotes) read the same value, drops duplicates, refuses unknown keys and blank required values, accepts only BOM-free UTF-8 sent as bytes and prints no value, an effective-value report that fails unless SLEEP_ENABLED is true and HEART_ENABLED is 0, check-only then install, verify by list-timers, journal and a posted gauge, rollback that stops both units and restores through a validated --restore), and says it was not run. The sleep tree is rolled out by diff and copy of that directory only.

Title: Manifest rows and the install identity
CodeSymbol: stack/ai-cli/ai-clis.manifest.tsv; provision-ai-clis.sh load_manifest, identity_of, compute_enabled, compute_needed
Detail: Fourteen tab-separated columns per row (key, version, needed_by, url, sha256, size_bytes, kind, tree, inventory, entry, version_cmd, version_regex, target, requires), '-' for none, comment lines allowed. A malformed row, a non-https URL, a non-hex hash or an unknown kind is exit 2. needed_by tokens are source:<name> (each a key of the feeder's SOURCE_READERS), service:ai-cli, service:ai-cli:openai, or required-by:<key> for a dependency. The needed set is the manifest crossed with the enabled consumers; service:ai-cli:openai is enabled only when an enabled ai-cli route is an OPENAI-family row in the registry at AI_CLI_REGISTRY. The effective account is AI_CLI_USER when AI_CLI_ENABLED is true, else AI_USAGE_USER_ACCOUNT, default homehub-ai; hub and root and invalid names are exit 2. Install identity is <version>-<sha12>-w<WRAPPER_REV>, plus -d<dep version>-<dep sha12> when requires is set (a dependency row itself is <version>-<sha12>); .complete is written last and recognition needs an exact match.

Title: Fetch, verify and extract safely
Detail: curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --proto =https --proto-redir =https --connect-timeout 20 --max-time 900, once per artifact. Size and sha256 are compared before any extraction. Archive members are listed first and refused when absolute, containing dot-dot, a device or fifo, a symlink or hardlink leaving the (stripped) tree after following the archive's own symlinks (a link to a link, or a member written through a link), or, for zip, any symlink; after extraction every link that landed must still resolve inside the staging root. Extraction is tar --no-same-owner (strip one level for nodetar, one named member for tree=member) or the validated Python zip extractor. Ownership is set through the chown seam (default root:root), modes are normalised to a-s,go-w,a+rX, and a single downloaded binary is made executable. Any failure removes the staging tree and the download immediately and keeps one reason.

Title: Whole-tree inventories
CodeSymbol: provision-ai-clis.sh PYARC inventory; manifest inventory column
Detail: After extraction every path in the row's inventory must exist (Codex: bin/codex, bin/codex-code-mode-host, codex-package.json, codex-path/rg, codex-resources/bwrap, codex-resources/zsh/bin/zsh; Gemini: gemini.js with all of its sibling chunk files). For a .js entry the static relative imports (import "./x.js", import ... from "./x.js", export * from "./x.js", at line start) are followed recursively and each must resolve to a file in the tree; comments and strings that merely mention an import do not count. The real Gemini 0.63.0 bundle (491 entries) and the pinned Node 22.20.0 were extracted with this check on 2026-10-11 under WSL and ran their --version (as root through a stand-in for runuser, not as the service account).

Title: Activation record, recovery and unrecorded links
Detail: activation = {state: pending|checked|committed, from, from_version, to, to_version, kind: activate|rollback} per key in state.json, where from_version may be the literal unobserved for a hand-installed predecessor that could not be run. link_txn is the one primitive used by activation and rollback: it writes pending durably first (a failed write aborts with no swap), swaps (ln -s temp then mv -T) and verifies the link, runs the check, writes checked, then committed; a failure at any later step restores the previous link, verifies it, and only then puts the earlier record back, and a restore that cannot be verified keeps the record and returns non-zero. Before the first write of a transaction the retry timer is armed through the SYSTEMCTL seam (a failure aborts with the link untouched), and the short timer lock is held from the arm through the durable pending write; a restore (revert or recovery) is accepted only when swap_to, including the bin-directory fsync, succeeded, otherwise the record is kept, the exit is 3 and the timer stays armed; recovery arms it before a restore. clis.<key>.baseline {target, version} is written once, in the pending write, when an unowned link is displaced and is never replaced; clis.<key>.history[<target>] {target, version} records the predecessor of exactly that target (written when an activation commits, never rewritten by a rollback, and a self-predecessor is ignored in favour of the baseline); a convergence that recognises an existing managed link takes the predecessor recorded for that exact target, else the baseline, never from null and never the target itself; rollback takes its target from the committed record, else the same history. Before committed is written the activated wrapper and its directory are fsynced, the staged tree is fsynced before publication, the publication directories after it, and the bin directory after every link change. A relative or aliased link target is normalised (realpath -m, relative to the bin directory) before it is compared with an install directory. A relative predecessor link is resolved against the bin directory when it is observed. recover runs at the start of every --run (before the off or empty-set early return) and handles only records in pending or checked: link at to and the check passes commits it; link at to and the check fails restores from (record kept if that fails); link still at from drops the record; any other link target is left alone. A link with no record is never touched, and a non-symlink at the bin path is reported and left alone. The AI_CLIS_DIE_AT seam kills the process with SIGKILL at pending, swap, check or checked so the tests exercise real crashes.

Title: The consumer check, one function, as the account
Detail: timeout ${AI_CLIS_CHECK_TIMEOUT:-20} $RUNUSER -u <effective account> -- env -i HOME=<fresh mktemp -d handed to the account> PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin <path> --version, then the first token matching the row's version regex must equal the expected version exactly ('*' accepts any token and is used only to roll back to a predecessor whose version could not be observed). The same function runs for staging (against a wrapper rendered for the staging tree), after the swap (through /usr/local/bin/<name>), in recovery and in rollback; the expected version is a parameter. A failure names the account and the exit code or the two versions.

Title: Rollback validates the previous version
Detail: --rollback KEY [--force-unverified] requires a committed record whose to equals the current link and runs the same link_txn as an activation with kind rollback: pending (from = the current link and its version, to = the recorded previous target) is written durably, the link is swapped (or, for a first install whose previous target is null, removed), and the check validates the previous version; a failing check restores the current install and exits 3. When the previous version was never observed the rollback is refused (exit 2) unless --force-unverified is given. A committed rollback record whose from is the install the manifest pins holds the key there (the next --run does not undo it) and counts as converged only while its link is still where the rollback put it, the most recent --run (or the rollback itself) passed the consumer check for that link target (a health stamp holding the target and the result), and the binary still exists and its version still runs as root; otherwise it is reported as unverified; a second rollback rolls forward and releases the hold; a changed pin releases it. Unknown keys, a key with no committed record, or a link that no longer matches the record are exit 2.

Title: Supervision, timer transitions and the non-blocking scheduler
CodeSymbol: stack/ai-cli/homehub-ai-clis-provision.service; homehub-ai-clis-provision.timer; provision-ai-clis.sh mode_schedule, mode_run, prepare_units, render_dropin
Detail: The service is Type=oneshot with TimeoutStartSec=3600 and ExecStart=/opt/homehub/stack/ai-cli/provision-ai-clis.sh --run; the timer is OnBootSec=5min and WantedBy=timers.target, installed disabled, with OnUnitInactiveSec supplied only by the drop-in interval.conf (an empty assignment first, then <N>min, N = AI_CLI_PROVISION_RETRY_MINUTES default 15 clamped 5..1440, non-numeric = 15). --install-units copies the two unit files from the script directory into AI_CLI_UNIT_DIR (default /etc/systemd/system) at mode 0644, runs daemon-reload only when something changed and enables or starts nothing; --schedule: no network; the same install step first (copy the units if they differ); render the drop-in; daemon-reload only when something changed; systemctl enable --now the timer; then systemctl start --no-block the service; it does not take the artifact lock, and when it needs to clear pending state it uses flock -n and defers if busy. --run: lock or exit 3; aggregate deadline 2400 s (AI_CLIS_DEADLINE_SECONDS seam); exit 0 runs disable --now on the timer unless a --schedule arrived during the run (compared by a durable stamp in the state directory), in which case the timer stays enabled and the exit is 3; exit 3 runs enable --now on it; AI_CLI_PROVISION=off or an empty needed set runs recovery first, then disable --now and clears pending (or keeps the timer and exits 3 when a transaction could not be reconciled). Unit and drop-in files are written atomically and a missing source or failed write makes --install-units exit 3 and --schedule exit 3 before the timer is enabled. The request stamp and the timer state are protected by a separate short lock (LOCK.timer): --schedule holds it for the stamp write plus the enable (a failed stamp write exits 3), a run holds it for the compare plus the disable, and neither holds it across a download. The timer is disabled only when no transaction for any CLI is pending or checked; --schedule with provisioning off or nothing needed first probes the main lock without waiting: if it is held the shutdown is DEFERRED (nothing is disabled, exit 0, the holder decides at its own end); otherwise, with an open transaction it starts the service (--no-block) so recovery runs, leaves the timer alone and exits 3. The fault-injection hooks (AI_CLIS_DIE_AT, FAIL_SAVE_AT, FAIL_RESTORE, FAIL_REMOVE, HOLD_IN_LOCK, FSYNC_LOG) are ignored unless AI_CLIS_TEST=1, which no unit sets. Unproven here: that systemd re-arms OnUnitInactiveSec after a oneshot that exited 3.

Title: Disk admission and cleanup
Detail: Before a download, free space (df -Pm on the nearest existing ancestor) on the temp directory and on the prefix must each be at least 3 x ceil(size_bytes in MiB) + 4096 MB (AI_CLIS_RESERVE_MB seam); otherwise the reason is 'low disk' and no download is attempted. Staging exists only under <prefix>/.staging, downloads only under <var tmp>/homehub-ai-clis, both removed on every failure, on EXIT and on TERM/INT/HUP; a run that holds the lock first deletes whatever an earlier crashed run left; a final-named directory without a matching .complete is moved into .staging and deleted, never reused, unless a link, a recorded transaction or another install's wrapper refers to it, in which case it is left in place and the pending reason says it is in use. The persisted reason never carries a measured figure; the free space is logged.

Title: state.json is minimal; the converged run writes nothing; the status contract
CodeSymbol: provision-ai-clis.sh load_state, save_state, note_pending, mode_status, mode_check
Detail: state.json is canonical JSON (sorted keys, two-space indent) rewritten by atomic rename only when its bytes would differ, and never created for an empty state. It holds per key the activation record, an optional pending {reason, since} (the only timestamp, set on first pending) and an announced hash so a pending message prints once per change. Writes are temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync, and a failed write is an error the caller must act on. --status opens the lock read-only and never creates it. A converged run (identity complete, link at its wrapper, record committed) makes no curl call and no filesystem write. --status prints PROVISIONING: complete, INCOMPLETE - <key>: <reason>; retrying every <N> min, running (the lock is held) or off; --status --json prints {provisioning, clis: {<key>: {installed, identity, version, link_target, activation_state, pending_reason}}} for every manifest key; --check exits 0 when converged and 3 otherwise. The shape is interface IF-038.

Title: Effective service account through all of setup-ai-usage.sh
Detail: AI_CLI_USER when AI_CLI_ENABLED is true else AI_USAGE_USER_ACCOUNT, applied to the usage unit's User/Group drop-in, the Codex-home ownership, REFRESH_HOME, every refresher drop-in (claude, claude2, gemini ReadWritePaths) and the printed recipes; one log line names it; two differing names no longer refuse. Built by branch feat-ai-cli-integration; this row is written by the registry owner from the plan and its symbols are the plan's names.

Title: ensure-ai-account.sh
Detail: Unprivileged-account creation and certification extracted from setup-ai-cli.sh: no sudo, no docker, a real shell; hub and root refused; called by first boot, setup-ai-cli.sh, setup-ai-usage.sh and the running-hub path. setup-ai-usage.sh creates an absent account instead of refusing.

Title: The Codex home is always created with the usage unit
Detail: /var/lib/homehub-ai-codex is created empty, owned by the effective account, mode 0700, whenever the usage unit is installed, regardless of AI_USAGE_SOURCES, because homehub-ai-usage.service lists it in ReadWritePaths; a CLI-only deployment installs no usage unit and references no Codex home. Asserted against the path read from the real unit file.

Title: First boot only schedules provisioning
Detail: When AI_USAGE_ENABLED or AI_CLI_ENABLED is true, first boot ensures the account and runs provision-ai-clis.sh --schedule, which returns promptly; it never runs --run in the foreground and a failure of the hook is a logged warning, never a failed first boot.

Title: Updater suppression files and their verification
Detail: The files carry exactly {"env":{"DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER":"1"}} and {"general":{"enableAutoUpdate":false}}; the provisioner's wrapper template exports the matching controls (TC-1202). Verification is by effective setting as the account where the vendor can report it, and recorded UNPROVEN where no query exists; a grep of the control name is not evidence.

Title: Credential-path mappings
Detail: claude <home>/.claude/.credentials.json; claude2 <home>/.claude-2/.credentials.json; gemini <home>/.gemini/oauth_creds.json; opencode <home>/.local/share/opencode/auth.json, with <home> the effective account's real home. Any other value is unsupported-path with the fix 'set <KNOB>=<default path>'; the word blank never appears because the feeder treats blank as unset. .env.example carries these defaults for every source it lists.

Title: Login-state matrix and no secrets
Detail: Run as the account with test -r/-s, content never read: login owed, permissions wrong (owner, mode and the exact chown/chmod; no recipe), credential present (not verified), verified (the feeder's last cycle logged live). Gemini additionally requires security.auth.selectedType = oauth-personal: missing is 'auth type not selected', anything else 'wrong auth type <x>'. A canary credential never appears in output and the happy path says none of missing, not found or refus.

Title: Per-consumer Codex status
Detail: The usage home /var/lib/homehub-ai-codex/auth.json is reported when codex is in AI_USAGE_SOURCES; the ai-cli home <home>/.codex/auth.json only when an OPENAI-family route is enabled (read from the real routes-enabled and registry); the two are never merged.

Title: Ring order and badges
Detail: Order claude, claude2, codex, grok, gemini, opencode, freellmapi filtered to AI_USAGE_SOURCES, unknown names appended in listed order; mark claude on claude and claude2; badges 1 and 2 only when both are listed. The order is read from gauges.js (USAGE_PROVIDER_ORDER) by the test; a missing sibling is a visible skip. Built by branch feat-gauge-rings-derive; this row is written by the registry owner from the plan.

Title: Hide makes membership follow the sources
Detail: The derived block is {slots, unlisted: hide, derivedFrom: AI_USAGE_SOURCES}; a source dropped from AI_USAGE_SOURCES leaves the slots on the next derivation; no FreeLLMAPI slot is added.

Title: Ownership rule for the source block
Detail: The source block is derivable only if absent, marker-carrying, or canonically equal to the shipped default {slots: [], unlisted: append}; anything else, including {slots: [], unlisted: hide}, is Owner-written and left alone with one log line; AI_USAGE_ENABLED=false leaves the output byte-identical to today's.

Title: Authority and inode safety
Detail: The source copy and the .env are the authority and the tool never edits the source; the destination is replaced by a rename inside its directory so the directory inode is unchanged; re-running is byte-identical.

Title: Output is non-lossy under the real normalizer and prints no secret
Detail: The derived block is passed through the real normalizeGaugeRings under node and compared slot for slot (no slot silently dropped); secret-class keys in the destination are never printed or logged.

Title: Presentation snapshot schema held to one fixture, both validators agree
Detail: The presentation snapshot schema is one fixture (presentation-v1.json) that both repositories validate. The image validator and the panel's validatePresentation agree on every case, the one known difference is pinned, and the fixture is byte-identical to the panel copy.

Title: Camera hierarchy truth table held to one fixture
Detail: The camera hierarchy's truth table is one fixture. The image's real power policy matches every row for keep_awake, the former Q5 rows (face unlock alone) expect false and pass, per the Owner's 2026-10-13 ruling, and the fixture is byte-identical to the panel copy.

Title: Runtime socket, state and cache paths agree between panel and image
Detail: Every panel source named in the runtime-paths fixture contains its path and the exported constants equal it; every image unit and script contains its path; the fixture is byte-identical to the panel copy.

Title: Audio vocabulary held to one fixture
Detail: Output positions, the levelled subset, the Bluetooth capability set and the volume-gesture vocabulary are one fixture. The image constants and documents match it, and the fixture is byte-identical to the panel copy.

Title: Door configuration defaults, shell validators and credential list agree via one fixture
Detail: The image's Door defaults, the firstboot shell validators and the credential list agree with door-config-v1.json. The firstboot validators run in bash: for every key the fixture marks shellValidated, they accept and reject the fixture's boundary values exactly; the other keys are not validated in shell, and the test pins that the shell accepts them.

Title: Touch filter defaults have one source: touchfilter.core.Policy
Detail: The renderer takes every default from touchfilter.core.Policy and emits only a TOUCH_* value that differs from it. A value equal to one of the four exact legacy image settings (min tap 60 ms, startup 1500 ms, longest gesture 10000 ms, 2048 points) is treated as unset, as the daemon's load-time migration treats it, so an older wall.env renders as a fresh one does. wall.env.example no longer sets those four. An operator's other value survives render and load. The effective policy on the panel is unchanged: 40 ms, 0 ms, 60000 ms, 8192 points.

Title: Public site inventory equals the panel's real site file set
Detail: ALLOWED_SITE_FILES equals the panel's real site file set (SITE_SOURCES plus the version and build-info stamps; the count is whatever the panel ships, 87 at OfficeWallNaglight c149439). A sibling test keeps the inventory exact.

Title: REQUIRED floor is a subset of the panel's capabilities manifest
Detail: Every floor capability and floor file the gate requires is declared by the panel's capabilities.json; the sibling test fails if the floor names something the panel does not declare.

Title: Legacy KMS is a named wall.env setting: legacy by default, explicit false selects atomic
Detail: WALL_DRM_LEGACY_KMS (default true, matching the live panel) is declared and documented in wall.env.example, including the way back. wall-firstboot.sh accepts exactly true or false, refuses anything else through fail_step, and carries the value into kiosk.env. wall-kiosk.sh exports WLR_DRM_NO_ATOMIC=1 for true, and for a missing, empty or invalid value (the default, logged when invalid); only an explicit false leaves the variable unset (atomic KMS), never exported as 0. wall-firstboot.sh installs the payload wall-kiosk.sh to /usr/local/bin on every run, so the paired release lane carries it; before 2026-10-14 only user-data did, and the deployed export never reached the running cage.

Title: Ubuntu's backlight save/restore is masked; wall-sleep.sh alone sets the boot brightness
Detail: wall-firstboot.sh masks the TEMPLATE systemd-backlight@.service, so every instance is masked whatever the hardware names its backlight, and logs it; a failed mask is a warning and firstboot carries on. Rationale: wall-sleep.sh owns the backlight (LLR-003, LLR-923), but systemd-backlight@ saves the level at shutdown and restores it at boot. A panel powered off inside the sleep window saved 0, and on 2026-10-14 its boot-time restore (raised to the systemd floor of 9 of 187) landed in the same second as wall-wake's full level and won, so the panel came up dim. Ordering wall-wake after the restore would need the hardware-specific instance name.

Title: Guard-owned relaunch schedule for the desktop S/PDIF leg
Detail: Backoff.next_delay(ran_for) resets to delays[0] when ran_for >= healthy_after, returns the current step and advances to at most the last step. supervise() loops run_once until a threading.Event is set, using Event.wait(delay) as the interruptible sleep. run_child() publishes the current child to the signal handler and terminates it if a stop landed before publication. wall-spdif-in.service passes --respawn --respawn-delays 1,2,4,8,16,30 --healthy-after 20; without --respawn the guard behaves exactly as before.

Title: A fresh install queues a non-blocking start of the AI CLI service after a successful setup
Detail: When setup-ai-cli.sh succeeds, firstboot runs systemctl start --no-block homehub-ai-cli.service so the API is up on the install boot rather than at the next reboot. The start is non-blocking because the unit is After=homehub-firstboot.service, and it is queued only on the success branch: a refused or failed setup starts nothing. A failed queue is a warning. Starting before the CLIs are provisioned is safe: the service resolves the CLI binary per launch.

Title: The weight feeder's setup retries itself until the tracker's data exists
Detail: setup-weight.sh exits 0 only when the feeder is installed AND the drop-in binds the one definitions file declaring WEIGHT_ITEM_CATEGORY; exit 4 means installed but the definitions directory or the category file is not there yet; exit 2 stays a broken configuration (blank knob, ambiguous category, a definitions path that exists and is not a directory). setup-weight.sh --retry runs the setup once more with one log line per attempt: 0 disables homehub-weight-setup.timer, 4 leaves it armed, anything else prints the reason, disables it and fails the unit. Every full run holds flock(1) on the root-owned /run/homehub-weight-setup.lock (fd kept through the timer decision, file never unlinked, wait 120 s under the service's 300 s TimeoutStartSec; a run that never got the lock exits 75, changes nothing and leaves the timer alone) for its whole life and settles homehub-weight-setup.timer itself from its own exit status (0 or a refusal/failure disarms, 4 arms), so firstboot and the retry service cannot interleave into data present, no bind, nothing retrying; setup installs the retry units. Firstboot only reports, and disables the timer when the knob is off. --check-only returns 4 for an absent directory or an absent category file. After WEIGHT_WAIT_WARN_AFTER (12) consecutive not-yet runs a warning naming WEIGHT_DEFINITIONS_DIR is logged at most once a day; there is no cutoff. The wait counter lives in root-owned /var/lib/homehub-weight-setup (not the feeder's state directory) and is replaced by rename, never written through a symlink. The timer fires every 15 minutes.
